outcomeNote: mishna dispute with a limiting clause

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְלָנָה עִמּוֹ בְּפוּנְדְּקִי, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט שֵׁנִי; וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט שֵׁנִי.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to «one who divorces his wife, and» afterward «she spent the night with him at an inn [befundaki], Beit Shammai say: She does not require a second bill of divorce from him, and Beit Hillel say: She requires a second bill of divorce from him,» since they may have engaged in sexual intercourse at the inn and thereby betrothed her once again.

segments.he: אֵימָתַי – בִּזְמַן שֶׁנִּתְגָּרְשָׁה מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין; וּמוֹדִים בְּנִתְגָּרְשָׁה מִן הָאֵירוּסִין – שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט שֵׁנִי, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לִבּוֹ גַּס בָּהּ.
segments.en: «When» did they say this halakha? «When she was divorced following» the state of «marriage.» Beit Hillel «concede that when she was divorced following» the state of «betrothal, she does not require a second bill of divorce from him, due to» the fact that «he is not accustomed to her.» Therefore, there is no concern that they engaged in sexual intercourse, even though they spent the night together at the inn.

moves.about: whether a divorcée who spent the night with her ex-husband at an inn needs a second get

moves.summary: only after divorce from marriage; Beit Hillel concede for betrothal

edges.about: whether a divorcée who spent the night with her ex-husband at an inn needs a second get
the dispute is only where she was divorced from full marriage, not from betrothal
a woman divorced from betrothal needs no second get, since he is not familiar with her

positions.claim: a second get is needed, except after divorce from betrothal
